Definition: Person has held at least one full-time position at a FAANG company.
Source Data: Organization legal name or short name matched against a curated list: Google, Amazon, AWS, Meta (Facebook, Instagram), Apple, Netflix, Alphabet.
Derivation Logic: If the normalized org legal name or short name matches the FAANG company list, the employment qualifies. All matching employment IDs are attached.

Definition: Person has worked full-time at a Fortune 500 company.
Source Data: Organization-level Fortune 500 highlight (set during Fortune 500 list ingestion from scraper source).
Derivation Logic: If the employer organization carries the Fortune 500 organization highlight the employment qualifies.

Definition: Person worked 12+ months at a company during its venture capital-backed phase, before any PE investment or exit (IPO/acquisition).
Source Data: Organization funding events mapped to VC backer type (Pre-Seed, Seed, Series A through Series J, Series Unknown).
Derivation Logic: For each employment \>= 12 months with an org that received VC funding: the VC funding must have occurred before any PE round, and the person's employment must end before the first IPO or acquisition. The employment must not have started after a PE backing date.
Key Business Rules: Employment must be \>= 12 months. VC phase only -- excludes periods after PE backing or exit.

Definition: Person worked 12+ months at a company during its private equity-backed phase (non-CxO role).
Source Data: Organization funding events mapped to PE backer type (Private Equity, Post-IPO Equity, Post-IPO Secondary, Post-IPO Debt).
Derivation Logic: If a PE funding event occurred before the employment end date and the person was not CxO-level they receive this highlight. Only awarded if the CxO variant does not apply.
Key Business Rules: Employment must be \>= 12 months. Superseded by PE-backed CxO Experience if person held CxO role.

Definition: Person held a CxO-level role at a PE-backed company for 12+ months. Supersedes the generic PE-backed Experience highlight.
Source Data: Same as PE-backed Experience plus job seniority = CxO.
Derivation Logic: Same PE funding logic but the person's seniority must be CxO. Also awarded if a CxO was employed during a VC-to-PE transition (they receive both VC-backed and PE-backed CxO highlights).
Key Business Rules: Employment must be \>= 12 months. Supersedes the generic PE-backed Experience highlight.

Definition: Person joined a company when it was at the early stage (Angel, Pre-Seed, Seed, or Series A) and the company raised additional funding during their tenure.
Source Data: Organization funding events; the most recent funding round at employment start determines stage. Early-Stage = Angel, Pre-Seed, Seed, Series A.
Derivation Logic: The org's stage at employment start must be Early-Stage Startup AND at least one additional funding stage event must have occurred during the employment.
Key Business Rules: Requires both: (1) early-stage at start AND (2) subsequent funding during tenure.

Definition: Person joined a company when it was at the mid stage (Series B or C) and the company raised additional funding during their tenure.
Source Data: Same as Early-Stage with different stage classification. Mid-Stage = Series B, Series C.
Derivation Logic: The org's stage at employment start must be Mid-Stage Startup AND at least one additional funding stage event occurred during the employment.
Key Business Rules: Requires both: (1) mid-stage at start AND (2) subsequent funding during tenure.

Definition: Person has worked at 3 or more distinct startup organizations.
Source Data: Organization stage at employment start. Startups = Early-Stage, Mid-Stage, or Late-Stage.
Derivation Logic: Count the distinct organization IDs where the org stage at employment start was Early-Stage, Mid-Stage, or Late-Stage Startup. If \>= 3 distinct orgs the highlight is awarded.
Key Business Rules: 3+ distinct startup orgs required. Multiple roles at the same startup count as one. [Industry] Veteran

Definition: Person demonstrates long-tenure loyalty: either one 10+ year employment or two or more 5+ year employments.
Source Data: Employment duration calculated from start/end dates.
Derivation Logic: Collect all full-time employments lasting \> 60 months (5 years). If the longest is \>= 120 months (10 years) OR there are 2+ such employments the highlight is awarded.
Key Business Rules: Threshold: one 10yr+ employment OR two 5yr+ employments.

Definition: Person was employed (non-leadership role) at a company that grew 2x or more in valuation during their tenure. Display value shows the highest integer multiplier achieved.
Source Data: Organization funding event valuations (post-money) during employment compared to valuation at employment start.
Derivation Logic: Compare valuation at employment start to peak valuation during employment. Down-rounds adjust the baseline downward. If highest_valuation / lowest_valuation \>= 2.0 the highlight is created with the floor of that multiplier. Only the single best growth highlight across all employments is kept.
Key Business Rules: 2x minimum. Only one growth highlight kept. Leadership variant takes priority. Down-rounds reset baseline.

Definition: Same as Employee Through Growth but the person held a leadership role (Founder, CxO, or VP-level). This variant takes priority over the employee variant.
Source Data: Same as Employee Through Growth plus leadership role check (Founder, CxO, VP-level).
Derivation Logic: Same valuation logic. If the person was in a leadership role the highlight uses Leadership Through {N}x Growth instead. A leadership highlight always supersedes an employee-variant highlight even at a lower multiplier.
Key Business Rules: Leadership variant always supersedes employee variant even at a lower multiplier.

Definition: Person was employed (non-CxO) at a company when it went through an IPO.
Source Data: Organization IPO funding events overlapping with employment dates.
Derivation Logic: If an IPO event date falls within the employment start-to-end window and the person's seniority is not CxO this highlight is awarded.
Key Business Rules: Non-CxO only. CxO roles get the CxO During IPO variant instead.

Definition: Person held a CxO-level role at a company when it went through an IPO.
Source Data: Same as Employed During IPO plus seniority = CxO.
Derivation Logic: Same IPO detection but seniority must be CxO. If a person has both CxO and non-CxO roles at the same org during IPO both highlights can coexist.

Definition: Person was employed (non-CxO) at a company when it was acquired. The acquirer name is included in the display value.
Source Data: Organization acquisition funding events with acquirer_organization_name.
Derivation Logic: If an acquisition event occurred during the employment and has an acquirer name the highlight is created. Multiple acquisitions by different acquirers produce separate highlights. Upgrades to CxO variant if any CxO employment overlaps.
Key Business Rules: Acquirer name required. Separate highlight per acquirer. Upgrades to CxO if applicable.

Definition: Person held a CxO-level role at a company when it was acquired.
Source Data: Same as Employed During Acquisition plus seniority = CxO.
Derivation Logic: Same acquisition logic. If any CxO employment at the org overlaps the acquisition the highlight is upgraded to the CxO variant for that acquirer.
Key Business Rules: CxO seniority required. Supersedes the Employed variant for the same acquirer.
